text:
anya: quick sanity from hydra-v2 bringup. int6-pertensor conversion shows recall@10 down ~2.1% vs fp16 on the docs-sampled slice. centroid drift looks larger week-over-week. anyone seen similar?

sam: which dataset/split and command?

anya: docs-sampled 3m (weekly). ran:
```
python eval_embeddings.py --model hydra-v2 --quant onnx-int6 --dataset docs-sampled --split weekly --metrics recall@1,5,10,centroid_shift
```
summary (aggregated):
- fp16: @1=0.525, @5=0.723, @10=0.805, centroid_shift=0.011
- int6: @1=0.518, @5=0.709, @10=0.784, centroid_shift=0.019

ravi: centroid_shift jump is suspicious. Did you apply global mean subtract + L2 norm?

anya: yes global mean from train. no per-week centering.

toni: try two things: 1) int6 per-channel calibration on stratified weekly sample, 2) PCA on weekly centroids to see if bias falls on PC1.

mlbot: eval-bot: queued job 81234 int6-perchannel calibrate (user=anya).

anya: also tested ensemble ordering: mean->quant vs quant->mean:
- fp16-mean @10=0.813
- mean->quant @10=0.792
- quant->mean @10=0.777
mean->quant seems best.

sam: that suggests quant noise isn't zero-mean across checkpoints. adopt avg-before-quant for multi-ckpt onboarding.

anya: interim (20m): int6-perchannel + PCA debias reduced centroid_shift to 0.012 and int6 @10 -> 0.797. reindexing HNSW with ef_construction=200 gave +0.004 more.

ravi: good. if stable across 4 weekly slices, make per-channel calibration + optional PCA-debias part of onboarding checklist. i'll help add scripts.

toni: note: if PCA debias generalizes poorly across domains, prefer to apply it at index-time only and keep it opt-in.

anya: agree. i'll run 4-week rolling check and drop artifacts into the model-onboard ticket.
